headline: Method B used 38% less base than Method A, but water source also differed (tap vs distilled) and the assumed cause (mixing time per addition) is contradicted.
station_summary: Assumed cause (mixing time per addition): not supported. Notable difference: water source. Temperature: within normal variation.

result.label: Base added at color flip
result.headline: Method B used 38% less base than Method A
result.explanation: Base added at color flip: 2.5 mL vs 4 mL in the control, a difference of -1.5 mL. Normal variation is ±1 (how far two runs normally differ, from 5 reference runs), so this is outside normal variation.

assumed_cause.text: Method B neutralized with less base because I stirred longer after each addition.
assumed_cause.label: contradicted
assumed_cause.statement: The assumed cause of longer stirring is contradicted because mixing time per addition was 4.8 s in Method B vs 4.4 s in Method A (difference of 0.4 s), which is within normal variation of ±0.7.

claims.text: Base added at color flip was 2.5 mL in Method B vs 4 mL in Method A, a difference of -1.5 mL, which is outside normal variation of ±1.
claims.label: observed

claims.text: Mixing time per addition was 4.8 s in Method B vs 4.4 s in Method A, a difference of 0.4 s, which is within normal variation of ±0.7.
claims.label: contradicted

claims.text: Water source was tap in Method B vs distilled in Method A, while the protocol specifies distilled and none of the 5 reference runs used tap.
claims.label: possible_explanation
claims.suggested_check: Repeat Method B with distilled water to match the control.

claims.text: Time to flip was 54.0 s in Method B vs 90.0 s in Method A (-36 s, normal variation ±22.4), and number of base additions was 5.0 additions vs 8.0 additions (-3 additions, normal variation ±2); both are consequences of the result.
claims.label: observed

claims.text: Liquid temperature (22.6 °C vs 21.6 °C), starting color a* (4.3 a* vs 3.9 a*), and air quality (122.1 raw vs 120.3 raw) were within normal variation; vinegar bottle (Bottle A), protocol steps performed, mixing per addition (3.0 inversions), sample volume (10.0 mL), dilution volume (20.0 mL), and indicator drops (3.0 drops) were identical.
claims.label: observed

claims.text: Base solution batch was not measured, so it cannot be ruled out as a factor.
claims.label: missing_evidence

claims.text: Air humidity was not measured, so it cannot be ruled out as a factor.
claims.label: missing_evidence

rejected_claims.text: Base solution batch was not measured in either Method B or Method A.

rejected_claims.text: Air humidity was not measured in either Method B or Method A.
rejected_claims.label: missing_evidence

follow_up.check: Matched rerun: repeat Method B exactly, but with water source set to distilled (as in the control). Optional swap run: repeat the control with water source set to tap.

outcomes.if: the base added at color flip returns to the control level (within normal variation)
outcomes.text: The difference is explained by water source, not by mixing time per addition.

outcomes.if: the base added at color flip stays as far from the control as before
outcomes.text: Water source is not the cause; the method difference is reproducible.
